name: Olga Velte

events.place: Brandon Mental Health Centre, Brandon, Manitoba, Canada

notes:
Olga Velte immigrated from Russia to Canada in 1923.  She lived with Mrs.
Edward Zelmer (Grandmother to Allan Zelmer) in her residence at 846 Aberdeen,
Winnipeg, until 1935.  She was admitted to Brandon Mental Hospital on June 13,
1935, and remained there until her death at 88 years of age.  She is buried in
Brandon Cemetery.  She died without leaving a will and the Public Trustee in
charge of her affairs was Patrick Beaman, Public Trustees Office, Winnipeg,
Wordsworth Building, Tel. 945-5093.  On September 29, 1992 he advised Allan
Zelmer that in 1966, for reasons of commencing Old Age Pensions, the Public
Trustees Office contacted the Soviet Consulate in order to obtain copies of
her birth documentation but further documents could not be traced.  Therefore,
aside from Ms. Veltes' stated birthdate, the birthplace could not be verified.
 Anyway, Pension benefits commenced and accumulated.  When she died, Garry
Steiman was established as the Administrator of the Estate and the legal firm
of Buchwald, Asper, Henteleff was engaged to trace family members who may be
eligible for distribution of the estate.  At this time (Oct,1992) this process
is ongoing.  The Public Trustee advised that for some periods of Olga's
institutionalization no charges were made for "board and room", while at other
times, very nominal charges were made against her assets.  She left an estate
of approximately $65,000.00.  The above information has been obtained from
Marilyn Fehr and Shawn Hughes of the legal firm on Sept. 28/92 and from
Patrick Beaman on Sept 29/92.
In the end, it was determined that under Manitoba Law, only the remaining
"first cousins" of the deceased would be entitled to distribution of her
estate.  Therefore, living first cousins such as Joyce Steiman, Arvid Zelmer,
Rose Schneider, Olga Lee, Beatrice Kahkonen and possibly a few others received
such distribution.
Lived most of her life in a hospital.
